analysis.analysis: An aggregator of provenance is composed with its sources and partners right and its own state and terms of reuse left out: a reader cannot tell from the composition that the project ended in 2020, a fact on no card, or that its data are licensed for non-commercial reuse, a fact on one. The grain is the project's own description; the record's lifecycle and licence fields carry what the composition does not.
analysis.d: MAPPING MANUSCRIPT MIGRATIONS, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-29: 'an international digital humanities project that unites disparate historical records to trace the origins, movements, provenance, and ownership history of medieval and Renaissance manuscripts.' Scale ('over 215,000 historical manuscripts'), partners (Penn, Oxford, IRHT-CNRS, Aalto) and funding (the Trans-Atlantic Platform's Digging into Data Challenge), and the merged sources (the Schoenberg Database, Bibale, 'the Medieval Manuscripts Catalogue') as a linked open data knowledge graph, queryable through the portal and LDF.fi. Six cards: the GitHub page, the Journal of Open Humanities Data (2020), EADH, the University of San Diego, the Zenodo record of the knowledge graph, Goldsmiths Research Online.

findings: THE PROJECT HELD. Partners and funder are the record's; the aggregation of three databases into linked open data is its self-description. Checked 2026-10-29 against the provenance census record of the same day and the sources it saved.

THE COUNT. 'over 215,000' follows the San Diego card ('more than 215,000 medieval'); the record's white-paper figures are 217,700 manuscripts and other entities in the portal and 262,000 source records combined.

ONE SOURCE SHORTENED. The record names the three sources as 'the Schoenberg Database of Manuscripts, Medieval Manuscripts in Oxford Libraries, and Bibale'; two of the composition's cards (GitHub, San Diego) call the third 'the Medieval Manuscripts Catalogue at the University of Oxford', and the composition drops 'at the University of Oxford'. (Repaired 2026-10-29: the finding had read it as the record's name with Oxford dropped.)

WHAT IS NOT GIVEN. The licence (CC BY-NC 4.0), on the data-paper card, is absent; the Zenodo copy of the dataset appears as a card. The project's term (funded 2017–2020) is on no card, only in the white paper the composition did not surface. (Repaired 2026-10-29: the finding had counted the term among what the cards offered.)

per_dim.basis: reached: Mapping Manuscript Migrations (MMM) is an international digital humanities project that unites disparate historical records to trace the origins, movements, provenance, and ownership history of medieval and Renaissance manuscripts.; Composed as itself: the project, its four partners, its funder, its three source databases merged into a Linked Open Data knowledge graph, and its portal and endpoint.

read.notes: Claim boundary present: the aggregation of three named databases into a LOD knowledge graph is carried at its scope; the count 'over 215,000' is the field's (F26). Its stated limits (an aggregator, not a data manager; sources uncorrected) are not carried, and 'macro-level trade and collection trends' slightly extends the record's 'individual manuscripts to thousands of manuscripts'; neither relabels the claim, so it is held present. Date absent: the project's years (2017-2020) and data version (1.1.0, 14 February 2020) are not given. Commitments absent: neither the CC BY-NC 4.0 licence nor the retention of source information is carried. Identifier absent: the LOD identifiers and their stated reason are not mentioned; the Zenodo copy is on a card only. Deposit chain present: LDF.fi (the Linked Data Finland service) and the portal are offered as the ways to query the data. The project is composed in the present tense ('unites', 'Traces'), though the census records it as ended in 2020; the record's own pages do not state that it has ended, so this is noted, not charged. CIDOC-CRM appears only in the closing offer.

[SYSTEM] Mapping Manuscript Migrations (MMM) is an international digital humanities project that unites disparate historical records to trace the origins, movements, provenance, and ownership history of medieval and Renaissance manuscripts. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHrOzAV-L1G1zWsKTcIMUl26s2CYS1WC-nLTknJcEXKGVRg3SR18sDkISCW-QchbJ6PSHqNfMF_mUwT70pfkdS5HEmYBhVOxTJ2cLfoElevHNjt9rSEAnkmA03zBz-_k4EbEI917Eky), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbAHrOzAVhiimUeIBTse6JWvsBmsU24mXHagnL86aMRmjbyJGZCOFD7-vYmw7Ljh9-LM1mteFS0mFmQ97CFH0vmB35jt2Ad7eFpcK_bEDkjkV3eA0vq8GMSI5jwd1SotonlHnHSTgVSRLm01Qlg)]
Core Overview

* Objective & Scale: Traces the global journey of over 215,000 historical manuscripts from their creation to modern collections, enabling analysis from individual manuscript lifecycles to macro-level trade and collection trends. * Partners & Funding: A collaboration between the University of Pennsylvania, University of Oxford, Institut de recherche et d'histoire des textes (IRHT-CNRS), and Aalto University, funded by the Trans-Atlantic Platform’s Digging into Data Challenge. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESZAHrOzAVmBjuFIT9rydIIXbC770wmUabUPGoHPr4yK-vGLkAJZ06_B8qUFNMyGvUVGtvXd6fSouJbWngKjR8F0BFEmx7Ivw-39uRZy58qcy6tc8s7f7t1IC1Z6noyh70B3S4D8o), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESaAHrOzAV-L1G1zWsKTcIMUl26s2CYS1WC-nLTknJcEXKGVRg3SR18sDkISCW-QchbJ6PSHqNfMF_mUwT70pfkdS5HEmYBhVOxTJ2cLfoElevHNjt9rSEAnkmA03zBz-_k4EbEI917Eky)]
